newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek Maillis plans two-for-10 scrip issue.
newsitem.headline: Greek Maillis plans two-for-10 scrip issue.

text.p: Greece's steel and synthetic strap producer Maillis will seek shareholder approval for a two-for-10 scrip issue at its forthcoming annual general meeting, it said in a statement.
Maillis intends to capitalise share premium and asset revaluation reserves totalling 3.28 billion drachmas.
Its 1996 pretax earnings rose 20.4 percent to 1,241 million drachmas on turnover growth of 18.2 percent to 10,273 million drachmas.
After-tax profit increased 30.7 percent to 991 million drachmas in 1996, exceeding earlier projections by 14 percent, the company said.
Management expects growth of 35 percent this year without taking into effect the favourable impact of the stronger U.S. dollar on exports.
The company exports a large portion of its output in the US dollar zone.

Maillis will distribute a dividend per share of 60 drachmas for fiscal 1996 versus 64 drachmas a year earlier and shares resulting from the 1.89 billion drachmas rights issue in September 1996 are entitled to the full dividend, it said.
Its 5.0 billion drachma, five-year business plan will see completion by end-1997, two years ahead of schedule, as market conditions in the sector have been favourable, Maillis said.
Total investments amounted to 4.0 billion drachmas in 1996 and are seen reaching 3.9 billion drachmas this year.
The 2.0 billion drachma investment in the industrial zone of Alexandroupolis in northern Greece is also expected to be completed in 1997, it said.
Maillis' shares gained 45 drachmas to 2,790 on Monday on volume of 15,830 shares. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
